title: Insurance Coverage for Individuals with Mental Health Conditions
what_it_is: Insurance Coverage for Individuals with Mental Health Conditions

sections.label: Bipolar disorder insurance questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how many under-35 Singaporeans have bipolar disorder and what appeal and assistance avenues exist for those declined insurance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) how many Singaporeans under the age of 35 are living with or have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder within the last three years; and (b) what avenues of appeal and assistance are available to young Singaporeans who encounter stigma from insurers or are declined insurance coverage due to their mental health condition, including bipolar disorder.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what avenues are available to patients who are unable to obtain medical insurance coverage as a result of their mental health condition; (b) whether the Ministry is considering a regulatory approach to address this concern; and (c) if so, what are the measures being considered.

sections.label: MediShield Life coverage
sections.summary: All Singaporeans and Permanent Residents are covered under MediShield Life regardless of pre-existing conditions, including mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: All Singaporeans and Permanent Residents are also covered under MediShield Life (MSHL), regardless of pre-existing conditions, including mental health conditions.

sections.label: Insurer underwriting fairness expectations
sections.summary: MOH and MAS expect insurers to deal fairly and not indiscriminately reject applications based on declared personal information such as medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In making underwriting decisions, insurers are fully expected by the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to deal fairly with their customers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For example, insurers should not indiscriminately reject an application solely on the basis of declared personal information, such as occupation, income, disability or medical condition, including mental health conditions.

sections.label: MAS action and appeals
sections.summary: MAS will act against insurers breaching its regulations or guidance, and individuals can appeal through their insurer's feedback channel or MAS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MAS will take action against insurers whose practices are in breach of MAS’ regulations or guidance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Individuals who have concerns over their insurer’s underwriting decision can make an appeal through their insurer’s feedback channel or through MAS.

sections.label: Further surveys and regulation work
sections.summary: Further surveys and studies will be conducted and released, and MOH and MAS continue working on regulating and guiding the insurance industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The short answer to both questions is yes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There will be further surveys and studies conducted and released, and MOH and MAS do continue to work together to see how we can appropriately regulate and guide the insurance industry to be able to provide these products in order to appropriately protect the public.
